    Ironcloak Vanguard¶

    [!INFO] The Forward Cloak — Nethra's Eyes Beyond the Wall The Ironcloak do not mass. They precede.

    History¶

    The Ironcloak Vanguard is the expeditionary cutting edge of the Ironcloak — the rebel tradition that claims descent from Socrates through Plato, the original Christians and Protestants, the American Revolutionaries, the libertarians, and finally the asteroid refugees who preserved humanity against the Shadows for three million years. The main Ironcloak body on Erisdar searches for the Archive of the Traveler inside the Ruins of Baoth; the Vanguard is the formation that operates beyond Erisdar, in the shadows of the Shadows' other holdings.

    Formally founded as the Vanguard in the scattering after the Great Divergence, its remit is the intercontinental: Merratodoni (where the Human Republic of Northeastern Merratodoni and the Merratodoni Liberty economy provide cover), Purification Lands-adjacent shipping, and the long watch on Eternal Paradise on Romanium Island — the Shadow base-state in the far NE where the Hybrians keep their most honest map. Vanguard cadres are small — a dozen at most — and led by a Lantern, a veteran who has read the fragmentary Nethrian Revelation and accepts that the goddess Nethra may walk among the Shadows themselves.

    The Vanguard's history is unwritten by design. Its victories are recorded as accidents in other nations' archives — a lighthouse that failed at the right hour, a ledger that burned clean.

    Patron¶

    Nethra — the Iron Goddess, a different kind of Shadow, daughter of Kirivis who survived his beheading by Rulfred and detonated the device that created Sea of Leviathan. Only the upper echelon knows she is worshipped at all; most Vanguard fighters think they fight for the idea of iron — endurance without worship. The Vanguard's upper cells know better and keep the secret because a goddess who is also a Shadow is a difficult prayer to teach.

    Its philosophical patron is the rebel lineage itself; Vanguard instruction begins with Socrates' trial and ends with the choice to board a ship that will not return.

    Sigil¶

    No sigil in the field — the Vanguard is the sigil's absence. When it must mark, it uses a plain iron-gray cloak, unbadged, the fabric weighted to hang without wind. The inverse — a burned Shadow eye — is cut into trees and left on doors to signal we were here, and the Shadow was not.

    Role¶

    Forward reconnaissance, sabotage, and deniable liberation. The Vanguard does not hold ground; it spoils it for the Hybrians. Its teams infiltrate through trade, especially via Demon's Horn and Beast's Bay, plant contradictions in colonial administrations (Anos Maloca, Anos Marti, Vennerian Channel outposts), and exfiltrate persons and relics the Shadows would rather keep. In Merratodoni its safe houses move with the caravans between Maemon and Luzia, and its signal is a cloak hung inside-out.

    Its signature tactic is the hollow day — a day where everything goes slightly right for the locals and slightly wrong for the master's tally — repeated until a colony decides the master's math is not worth the cost.

    Relation to Currencies & Regions¶

    The Vanguard carries no standard coin — carrying one standard is how you are caught. Its logistics run on whatever is local: Merratodoni Liberty in Merratodoni (its most honest home, silvered with Romanium promise), Erilia on Erisdar, Vennerian Ducat and Anosi Mark at sea, Demonic Ember when it must deal through Demon's Horn, and Meblean Pearl when diplomats are the mark (pearls are forgettable because they are beautiful). Its hard reserve is Romanium itself — raw, unminted, the one resource all of the Shadows' empires must account for and therefore the hardest to counterfeit as story.

    A Vanguard cadre that cannot change its money is a cadre that has already been made.
